label: Figure 1
manuscript_caption_or_title: Figure 1. Task-matched validation framework for nighttime lights as a socioeconomic proxy. Spatial representation and annual-change alignment provide within-year diagnostics. Out-of-sample validation distinguishes stand-alone temporal transfer from conditional incremental value. The conditional test compares an intercept-recalibrated historical GDP benchmark with the same benchmark augmented by light. Arrows connect validation questions, not causal steps or prerequisites; earlier evidence does not establish later validity. Geographic diagnostics and product, model-form, and temporal-domain checks support both out-of-sample questions. Calibration uses preceding GDP outcomes; target-year light is observed, while target-year GDP is excluded from calibration. The lower strip identifies the task-specific validation conditions.

label: Figure 3
manuscript_caption_or_title: Figure 3. Continuous pre-COVID out-of-sample temporal-transfer skill relative to the national training-period mean. Each point is comparative Skill R² = 1 − SSE(light)/SSE(B0) for a light-to-GDP calibration estimated only on preceding GDP years and applied to observed target-year light. Positive values favor the stand-alone light mapping; negative values favor B0. Target-year GDP is excluded from calibration, but target-year light is observed, so the exercise is temporal measurement transfer rather than a pure ex ante forecast. The five folds cover target years 2015–2019 and use identical GDP test rows across products within year.

label: Figure 4
manuscript_caption_or_title: Figure 4. Geography of continuous pre-COVID temporal-transfer loss relative to the national training-period mean. Each panel maps a prefecture's mean standardized excess squared loss averaged across its available transfer folds in 2015–2019; negative values favor the stand-alone light mapping and positive values favor B0. Both panels use the same continuous scale centered at zero and the accepted current-boundary set. The mapped quantity is comparative benchmark-relative performance, not sensor error alone.
